title: wasmtime
description: The Bytecode Alliance reference runtime; powers server-side WASM with a Cranelift compiler and component-model support. It is implemented in Rust, supports WASI 0.2 / component model, and is released under Apache-2.0.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Wasmer
description: A universal runtime shipping a package manager (WAPM) and multiple compilers including Singlepass for fast startup. It is implemented in Rust, supports WASI 0.1/0.2, and is released under MIT.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: WAMR
description: The WebAssembly Micro Runtime targets tiny devices with an interpreter plus AOT modes that fit in kilobytes of RAM. It is implemented in C, supports WASI, and is released under Apache-2.0.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: WasmEdge
description: A CNCF sandbox project tuned for edge and serverless with TensorFlow and image extensions for AI workloads. It is implemented in C++, supports WASI 0.1/0.2, and is released under Apache-2.0.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: V8
description: Chrome and Node ship V8 with Liftoff (fast baseline) and TurboFan (optimizing) tiers compiling WASM at near-native speed. It is implemented in C++, supports n/a (browser + Node experimental), and is released under BSD-3-Clause.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: SpiderMonkey
description: Firefox’s engine compiles WASM with Cranelift-derived Ion pipelines and was first to ship WASM threads. It is implemented in C++/Rust, supports n/a (browser), and is released under MPL-2.0.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: JavaScriptCore
description: Safari’s engine runs WASM through its BBQ and OMG tiers, sharing the JIT infrastructure with JavaScript. It is implemented in C++, supports n/a (browser), and is released under LGPL-2.1 / BSD.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: wasm3
description: A high-performance interpreter that runs WASM on microcontrollers where JIT compilation is impossible. It is implemented in C, supports WASI (minimal), and is released under MIT.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: WAVM
description: A research-grade runtime with a focus on spec compliance and a custom LLVM-based optimizing backend. It is implemented in C++, supports WASI, and is released under BSD-3-Clause / LLVM exception.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: wasmi
description: Parity’s interpreter-first runtime, designed for deterministic execution in blockchain-adjacent hosts. It is implemented in Rust, supports WASI (via host), and is released under MIT/Apache-2.0.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: GraalWasm
description: Oracle’s Truffle-based WASM engine lets WASM call into JVM languages and vice versa polyglot-style. It is implemented in Java, supports WASI, and is released under GPL-2.0 with Classpath Exception.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Extism
description: A plug-in framework wrapping wasmtime so any language can load WASM plug-ins through one stable PDK. It is implemented in Rust (host SDKs many), supports WASI (sandboxed), and is released under BSD-3-Clause.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Chicory
description: A pure-Java, zero-native-dependency WASM interpreter for JVM hosts that cannot ship native code. It is implemented in Java, supports WASI preview1, and is released under Apache-2.0.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: WasmKit
description: A TypeScript toolkit for inspecting and running WASM modules with a focus on developer ergonomics. It is implemented in TypeScript, supports WASI (partial), and is released under MIT.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Lucet
description: Fastly’s retired ahead-of-time runtime that pioneered WASM at the CDN edge before WasmEdge-era designs. It is implemented in Rust, supports WASI 0.1, and is released under Apache-2.0 / BSD.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.
